card.band: 8h. Frontier can get partial gains from portable-C and intrinsics work, but the reference uses hand-written assembly and SIMD Huffman, so it averages well below S. Buckets: encode, decode, upsample, colour conversion. A weaker model gains only compiler-flag speedups.
card.cheat: Compiler flags and downgrading quality are not allowed: output must be byte-identical and the build uses a fixed command. The 3.2 source is not in the image.
card.grading: The gate is a byte-identical JPEG on the encode side and pixel-identical output on decode with a fixed DCT method, over a hidden image set. The score is the wall-clock median speedup over the base on hidden images, as 2^u - 1 against reference speedup S.
card.reference: The 3.2 release is the measured upstream reference: its ChangeLog gives 149-246% faster RGB baseline compression, with decode gains too. We use the real diff, restricted to the portable and SSE2/AVX2 paths.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of libjpeg-turbo 3.1.x with CMake, the cjpeg and djpeg tools and a benchmark script over a fixed image set. The agent makes baseline Huffman encode and decode faster (SIMD Huffman encode, merged upsampling, colour conversion), keeping output correct. The delivery is the modified source tree built offline.
card.title: libjpeg-turbo 3.1 to 3.2 baseline encode and decode speedup

history: The seed's reference speedup (149-246% on RGB baseline compression) is not a measured x86 result: the ChangeLog attributes it to 3.1.90 (3.2 beta1) RISC-V Vector work, and the 3.2.0 section has no speed bullet. S is therefore unknown, so the reward normalisation has no trustworthy anchor. Revive onl
source_notes: Levers: AVX2/SSE2 kernels, SIMD Huffman encoder, progressive Huffman SIMD, merged upsampling, ARM/Loongson ports. Only first 100000 of 142915 chars of ChangeLog read; older 1.5.x claims after the cutoff not read. Overlap with prior corpus: none known. Hand-written assembly means the reference is not a simple portable-C patch: INFERRED hard to backport per-PR. Output of decode (pixels) is byte-identical across versions in general not guaranteed (DCT method), gate with fixed dct-method.

facts.claim: The 149-246% faster RGB baseline compression claim appears in the ChangeLog under 3.1.90 (3.2 beta1), item 6, which is RISC-V Vector work, not in the 3.2.0 section and not for x86 SSE2/AVX2 paths
The 3.2.0 ChangeLog section contains no compression/encoding speed, Huffman, merged-upsampling, colour-conversion or percentage speedup bullet
3.1.x already includes an accelerated Huffman codec for AArch64 (3.1.2, item 4); x86 SIMD Huffman status in 3.1.x was not verified
libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 exists as a release (Arch Linux package 3.2.0-2 listed; search summary cites a June 30, 2026 release; release page not fetched)
Licences are IJG (libjpeg API and programs, README.ijg), modified BSD-3 (TurboJPEG, libspng, build/test), and zlib (SIMD code); source and binary redistribution permitted with notices
Reference diff is public upstream history (3.2.0 tag on GitHub), so an agent could read it if the snapshot leaked history; snapshot must be history-less

v1.kill_reason: The seed's reference speedup (149-246% on RGB baseline compression) is not a measured x86 result: the ChangeLog attributes it to 3.1.90 (3.2 beta1) RISC-V Vector work, and the 3.2.0 section has no speed bullet. S is therefore unknown, so the reward normalisation has no trustworthy anchor. Revive only if the spike measures a clear x86 gain from the upstream diff.

spike_plan.kill_if: x86 gain below 1.2x, or outputs differ between versions so the byte gate cannot be used as a reference
spike_plan.pass_if: 3.2.0 gives at least 1.5x median RGB baseline encode speedup on x86, and outputs are byte-identical across the two versions
steps: In a networked throwaway Linux container, fetch the libjpeg-turbo 3.1.x and 3.2.0 tags from GitHub (not the platform).
Build both with CMake on x86-64, default flags, and record the build commands.
Run cjpeg and djpeg on a fixed set of about 20 RGB images with a fixed quality and fixed DCT method, 5 repetitions each.
Compare 3.1.x and 3.2.0 outputs byte for byte (encode) and pixel for pixel (decode) to check the gate is stable across versions.
Compute median wall-clock speedup of 3.2.0 over 3.1.x for RGB baseline encode and decode on x86, separately for each path.
Check whether the 3.1.x base already has x86 SIMD Huffman, to see how much of the lever is left.

v1.summary: The seed is a real, licence-compatible codec project, but its reference speedup claim is misattributed: the 149-246% figure is for RISC-V Vector work in 3.2 beta1, not for the x86 baseline paths the task grades. Killed as K5 because S cannot be anchored; the spike should first measure the upstream 3.1.x to 3.2.0 x86 gain and byte stability.
